note: What the Sign-in template does, checked headless: affrescoui test sign-in.scenarios.json

scenarios.name: sign-in
scenarios.note: A valid email and a password of 8 characters or more sign in and greet the user by email

scenarios.name: errors-show-only-after-submit
scenarios.note: Each step checks its own field only when it is submitted: the email on Continue, the password on Sign in.

expect.text: Enter a full email address, like name@example.com

scenarios.name: fixing-a-field-clears-its-error
scenarios.note: After a failed sign-in, correcting the email removes its error at once while the password's stays

scenarios.name: go-to-create-account-and-back
scenarios.note: The link opens the create-account screen without old errors; its back link and Escape return to sign in

scenarios.name: create-an-account
scenarios.note: Create account needs a name too; with all four fields valid (the password confirmed) it signs in

scenarios.name: sign-out
scenarios.note: Signing out returns to sign in with the email kept and the password cleared

scenarios.name: enter-signs-in
scenarios.note: Enter anywhere in the card signs in, like the button

scenarios.name: switch-the-theme
scenarios.note: The moon button and Cmd+J switch between the light and the dark tokens

scenarios.name: show-and-hide-the-password
scenarios.note: The password is a secret field until the eye is pressed; the eye's name says what it does

scenarios.name: the-focused-field-is-marked
scenarios.note: Focusing a field remembers which one, for its accent border

scenarios.name: remember-me
scenarios.note: Remember me is on by default; the box or its text turns it off, and the signed-in card says so

expect.text: You will be signed out when you close the app

scenarios.name: reset-the-password
scenarios.note: Forgot password? asks for the email (prefilled), checks it and says the link was sent

expect.is: Enter the email of your account
We sent a reset link to ada@example.com

scenarios.name: cancel-the-reset
scenarios.note: Escape closes the reset dialog and sends nothing

scenarios.name: password-strength
scenarios.note: The meter follows passwordStrength: length and variety (capitals, digits, symbols); the hint says what to add

expect.text: Use 12 or more characters: capitals, digits, symbols
Add more characters, a capital, a digit, and a symbol

scenarios.name: welcome-after-creating
scenarios.note: A new account is greeted by name in a toast and an initial

scenarios.name: escape-keeps-the-session
scenarios.note: Bug: Escape after signing in went back to the sign-in form while still signed in

scenarios.name: escape-after-signing-out
scenarios.note: Bug: after signing out, Escape went back to the signed-in screen

scenarios.name: keyboard-only-sign-in
scenarios.note: Bug: links and buttons could not be reached by Tab. Signs in with the keyboard alone: Tab, Space and Enter

expect.text: You will be signed out when you close the app

scenarios.name: enter-runs-the-focused-control
scenarios.note: Bug: Enter on a focused link or button in the card signed in instead of running it

scenarios.name: tab-reaches-the-top-bar
scenarios.note: Bug: the theme button could not be focused and had the text role; the top bar is reached by Tab and named

scenarios.name: fields-are-named-and-errors-announced
scenarios.note: Bug: fields were named by their placeholder, and errors had no role or description

expect.is: Enter a full email address, like name@example.com

scenarios.name: smallest-window
scenarios.note: Bug: at the smallest window the create card with its errors ran past the window and over the footer; the card fits its content and is centred, so the email step's card is shorter than the password step's

scenarios.name: resizing-relays-out-at-once
scenarios.note: Bug: sizes worked out in computed values kept the old window size until the next click, so the first click after a resize hit the wrong field; the card fits its content and is centred, so the email step's card is shorter than the password step's

scenarios.name: full-screen
scenarios.note: At 1920 by 1080 the card stays 420 wide in the middle, with the logo and the footer

scenarios.name: sign-in-light-theme
scenarios.note: The light theme: a white card on a pale background (the toggle's name, with its key as each platform writes it, is in tests/unit/automation.cpp)

scenarios.name: dark-theme
scenarios.note: The dark theme from the moon button: a deep card on a dark background, and back with Cmd+J (Ctrl+J off macOS)

scenarios.name: italian
scenarios.note: The IT chip switches every text to Italian, errors included

expect.text: Inserisci un indirizzo email completo, come nome@example.com

scenarios.name: sign-in-arabic-right-to-left
scenarios.note: Cmd+L twice switches to Arabic: the texts are Arabic and the layout runs right to left

expect.text: أدخل عنوان بريد إلكتروني كاملًا، مثل name@example.com

scenarios.name: shortcut-keys-are-readable
scenarios.note: Bug: the keys were shown as the symbols for Command and Shift, which the screen's font has not got, so they read as question marks. The keys with the platform's modifier read differently on each one: tests/unit/automation.cpp checks them

scenarios.name: commands-and-shortcuts
scenarios.note: F1 lists the commands with their keys; the shortcuts show the password, slow the network and sign out

scenarios.name: unknown-account-then-a-known-one
scenarios.note: The fake server knows ada@ and sam@ only: an unknown email stops at Continue, a known one goes on to the password (it takes any long-enough password until one is set, as in account-settings)

expect.text: No account uses this email. Check it, or create one.

scenarios.name: two-step-wrong-code
scenarios.note: Sam has two-step on: a wrong code is refused and announced, the right one signs in

expect.text: Enter the 6-digit code we sent to sam@example.com
That code is not right. Check it and try again.

expect.is: That code is not right. Check it and try again.

scenarios.name: labels-stay-clear-after-two-step
scenarios.note: Bug: after a wrong code, the account page drew the Email label as a purple bar: it took the colour of the Verify button drawn in its place

scenarios.name: dialog-fields-have-quiet-borders
scenarios.note: Bug: the fields of the change password dialog had no border colour and were drawn with a black frame

scenarios.name: resend-countdown
scenarios.note: A new code can be asked for after 30 seconds; the link counts down

expect.is: We sent a new code to sam@example.com

scenarios.name: reset-with-a-code
scenarios.note: The reset link's code and a new password, confirmed, replace the password; the old one stops working

expect.text: Open the link we sent to ada@example.com, or enter the code in it
That code is not right. Check it and try again.

expect.is: Your password was changed. Sign in with the new one.

expect.text: The email or the password is not right.

scenarios.name: confirm-and-length-limits
scenarios.note: The confirmation must match the password, and the fields stop at their maxLength

scenarios.name: slow-network-busy-states
scenarios.note: With Slow network on, the button shows the work, is disabled and the status line announces it

scenarios.name: provider-sign-in
scenarios.note: Continue with Example ID waits for the fake provider; its answer, played as an event, signs in

scenarios.name: provider-failure-and-cancel
scenarios.note: A failed answer is shown as an alert; once cancelled, a late answer is ignored

expect.text: Example ID could not sign you in: access denied

scenarios.name: session-expires
scenarios.note: The session counts down; a minute before the end a toast offers more time, then the sign-in form says it expired

expect.is: Your session ends in a minute

expect.text: Your session expired. Sign in again to go on.

scenarios.name: stay-signed-in
scenarios.note: Stay signed in, from the card, gives the session five more minutes

expect.is: You stay signed in for 5 more minutes

scenarios.name: account-settings
scenarios.note: The account page saves the name and email, turns two-step on (click or Space) and changes the password

expect.text: The email or the password is not right.

scenarios.name: account-errors
scenarios.note: Saving an empty name or a wrong email shows the field errors on the account page

expect.text: Enter a full email address, like name@example.com
This email is already on your account

scenarios.name: identifier-first
scenarios.note: Continue looks the email up first; the password step names the account in a chip, its initial and its email trimmed, and asks for nothing else

scenarios.name: caps-lock-warning
scenarios.note: A key typed with caps lock on, in the password, shows a warning under it; a key without caps lock, or leaving the field, hides it

scenarios.name: not-you-goes-back-to-the-email
scenarios.note: "Not you?" on the password step goes back to the email, keeps it to edit, clears the password and focuses the email

expect.text: Enter the 6-digit code we sent to sam@example.com

scenarios.name: username-is-checked
scenarios.note: A username is checked as it is typed: a spinner while checking, then taken, available or invalid

scenarios.name: create-waits-for-the-username-check
scenarios.note: Creating while the name is still being checked asks to wait

expect.text: Wait for the check to finish

scenarios.name: terms-are-required
scenarios.note: The account is not created until the terms are agreed

expect.text: Agree to the terms to continue

scenarios.name: invitation-code
scenarios.note: An invitation code is checked, and a known one names the team

expect.text: That code is not known. The demo code is EXAMPLE-INVITE.
Sam invited you to Example Team

expect.is: Welcome, Jon Doe. You joined Example Team.

scenarios.name: email-is-verified-before-sign-in
scenarios.note: A new account gets a 6-digit email code; a wrong one is refused, and going back keeps the form

expect.text: That code is not right. Check it and try again.

scenarios.name: password-rules-tick-off
scenarios.note: Each password rule is ticked off, for the eye and for a screen reader

scenarios.name: create-starts-with-an-empty-password
scenarios.note: The password typed to sign in is not carried into a new account

scenarios.name: setup-wrong-code-then-right
scenarios.note: Turning two-step on: a short or wrong app code is refused in the dialog, the right one moves on to the backup codes, which must be ticked as saved. Back returns to the app code with the dialog still open (it used to close it)

expect.text: Tick the box once the codes are saved

scenarios.name: text-me-a-code
scenarios.note: Sam asks for a text instead: the title and caption change, a toast confirms the made-up number, and the same demo code signs in

expect.text: Enter the 6-digit code we texted to 555-0142

scenarios.name: backup-code-is-used-once
scenarios.note: A wrong backup code is refused; a right one signs in, is struck off the list and cannot be used again

expect.text: That backup code is not right, or it was already used

scenarios.name: trust-this-device-skips-the-code
scenarios.note: Ticking Trust this device remembers it for 30 days: the next sign-in skips the code, until the device is removed on the account page

expect.is: Device removed. It will be asked for a code again

expect.text: No trusted devices: every sign-in asks for a code

scenarios.name: new-backup-codes
scenarios.note: With two-step on, New codes opens the codes step straight away, refills the list and says the old codes stop working

expect.is: New backup codes are ready. The old ones no longer work

scenarios.name: lock-after-five
scenarios.note: Five wrong passwords lock the account; resetting the password unlocks it

scenarios.name: reset-unlocks
scenarios.note: A finished reset clears the failures, so the new password signs in

scenarios.name: reset-code-expires
scenarios.note: The emailed code lasts 10 minutes; after that it is refused until a new one is sent

scenarios.name: step-up
scenarios.note: Two minutes after signing in, changing the password asks for it again first

expect.is: ada.home@example.net is now your primary email
We sent a link to ada.new@example.com: open it to verify the address
Passkey added. You can use it at your next sign-in
Every other device was signed out

expect.text: That isn't DELETE. Type it exactly
